title: Marketing Decisions and AI-Assisted Coding
objectives: Specify an action, observation unit, information set, and outcome horizon.
Translate a small marketing calculation into readable Python.
Verify generated code using identities and counterexamples.

slides.title: A Merchant Chooses a Market
slides.description: A merchant consults a laptop and ledger while two boats travel toward different customer markets. The landscape represents a choice under incomplete information.
slides.notes: A useful analysis connects the available evidence to a feasible decision. Different markets can require different products, margins, and forecasts.
slides.source: Original conceptual illustration. 05_Slides/assets/PROVENANCE.md.

slides.title: A Renewal Offer
bullets: A subscription firm can contact 5,000 eligible customers.
The decision concerns incremental contribution over the next 30 days.
Past spending, consent, and account history are available before contact.
slides.notes: The contact budget constrains the action. A high predicted renewal rate can reflect customers who would renew without an offer. The target must include the additional contribution caused by contact.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Analytical Questions
bullets: Description: how often do customers renew?
Prediction: who is likely to renew?
Causal effect: how does an offer change renewal?
Decision: which contacts generate positive incremental contribution?
slides.notes: The same customer records can support different analytical objects. Predictive performance evaluates forecasts under the represented conditions. A targeting policy also needs the untreated comparison and relevant costs.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Incremental Contribution
slides.intro: For account $i$, compare renewal under an offer and no offer.
slides.interpretation: Contribution $m_i$ and contact cost $c_i$ are dollars per account over the stated horizon.
slides.notes: The formula assumes that the offer cost can be summarized by c and that contribution already deducts relevant variable costs. A discount paid on every treated purchase requires an additional cost term.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Response and Incremental Value
slides.caption: Synthetic accounts. Contribution is 100 dollars and contact cost is 3 dollars.
slides.description: Account A has treated renewal probability 0.91 and incremental contribution -2 dollars. Account B has probability 0.50 and contribution 7 dollars.
slides.notes: A rises from 0.90 to 0.91. B rises from 0.40 to 0.50. The untreated probabilities explain the reversal. These probabilities are imposed teaching inputs.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: The Observation Unit
bullets: A product line, order, customer, and customer-month are different units.
The key identifies one row at the intended level.
Aggregation changes the weights used in an average.
slides.notes: A customer with five order lines receives five times the weight of a customer with one line in a line-level mean. Define whether the managerial comparison concerns orders or equally weighted customers.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Python Objects and Order Totals
slides.intro: Three synthetic product lines belong to two orders.
slides.code:
lines = [('A', 2, 10), ('A', 1, 5), ('B', 1, 12)]
orders = {}
for order, quantity, price in lines:
    orders[order] = orders.get(order, 0) + quantity * price
total = sum(orders.values())
aov = total / len(orders)
assert (total, aov) == (37, 18.5)
slides.check: Check: total sales are 37 dollars and average order value is 18.50 dollars.
slides.notes: The tuple stores an order ID, a quantity, and a unit price. The dictionary accumulates sales by order. The denominator is two orders. Dividing by the three lines gives average line sales.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Functions and Data Contracts
bullets: Inputs have names, types, units, and allowed missing values.
A function returns a defined output and an exception report.
Returns, canceled orders, and duplicate lines need explicit rules.
slides.notes: A numeric-looking string requires conversion before arithmetic. A negative quantity may be a legitimate return. A rule should preserve a trace from the original record to its inclusion or exclusion.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: A Duplicate Lookup Doubles Sales
slides.caption: Synthetic join. One 40-dollar order matches two customer records.
slides.description: The original order has one row. A duplicate customer lookup produces two joined rows and an apparent 80-dollar total.
slides.notes: A many-to-one relationship requires unique customer keys in the lookup. Check key uniqueness before merging and reconcile sales afterward.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: An AI Coding Request
bullets: Return one row per order and an exceptions table.
Treat negative quantities as returns under the stated rule.
Verify the 37-dollar example and reject missing order IDs.
Explain each transformation before adding the next step.
slides.notes: A useful request specifies analytical behavior and acceptance criteria. The assistant can propose an implementation while the analyst remains responsible for the observation unit and sample rules.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Code Errors and Missing Evidence
bullets: A repeated daily total requires a correction to aggregation.
Unrecorded food requires additional measurement or a recorded-behavior target.
A coupon decision needs evidence about untreated outcomes.
slides.notes: The response to a failed analysis depends on the unresolved distinction. Ask for the smallest check that could distinguish a calculation error from missing information. A new model can improve implementation while leaving the missing-information problem unchanged. A validated category summary can also remove unnecessary prose generation when the decision only needs category totals.
slides.source: Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes, M1 §1.12.

slides.title: Verification With Counterexamples
bullets: A duplicate lookup must trigger a failed key check.
An unmatched customer must remain visible in the assessment.
An empty input needs an explicit result.
Order totals must reconcile with eligible product lines.
slides.notes: These checks test properties that can fail even when code runs. Repeating the program with the same input confirms reproducibility but does not independently establish correctness.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: mHealth Records
bullets: Food entries describe recorded items on observed user-days.
The separate daily table covers only part of the food-log history.
Reported daily calories repeat across item rows.
slides.notes: The released records replace user identifiers and birthdays and perturb weight values. The source daily total is distinct from the sum of item calories. Neither is a direct measure of complete usual intake.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.8, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Join Choice Changes the Sample
slides.caption: Released mHealth cohort: 76,804 observed user-days.
slides.description: A left join retains all 76,804 user-days. Only 37,634 match the separate daily file, leaving 39,170 unmatched.
slides.notes: An inner join would remove more than half the cohort days. Missing calendar days are separate from unmatched rows in a join. The fixed cohort rule preserves within-user histories.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.8.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Coding Exercise: An Order Assessment
bullets: Implement aggregation with a coding assistant.
Add a return, a missing identifier, and a duplicated lookup key.
Report how each change affects rows, totals, and exceptions.
slides.notes: Use the small example in ../03_Data_and_Code/Lecture_Examples/session_examples.py S01. Retain the original three-line example as a hand-check. The output should distinguish accepted records from records requiring a decision.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Versioned Evidence
bullets: Record the model, date, prompts, tools, settings, parser, and scoring rule.
Keep known failure cases and evaluate transfer on fresh cases.
Check parsing, execution, and analytical correctness separately.
slides.notes: A historical finding concerns the tested configuration. A current workflow can differ through the model, interface, data, or judgment rule. Chen, Zaharia, and Zou separate code formatting from correctness after postprocessing. A code generator can improve on one measure while an automated pipeline breaks on another.
slides.source: M1 §1.13. Chen, Zaharia, and Zou (2024), §3.5. https://hdsr.mitpress.mit.edu/pub/y95zitmz/release/2 ../01_Resources/14_LLM_Evidence_and_Revalidation/README.md

slides.title: A Reproducible Analysis
bullets: Relative paths identify inputs and outputs.
A fresh run reconstructs results without hidden notebook state.
Record package versions and consequential AI contributions.
slides.notes: A random seed reproduces a particular random computation under a given implementation. It does not establish valid sampling or eliminate changes across software versions.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: A Campaign Specification
bullets: Define the eligible customers and contact date.
State the contribution horizon and relevant costs.
Identify the evidence needed for the untreated outcome.
Choose a numerical check that would reveal a wrong denominator.
slides.notes: The specification should state one feasible action and the comparison that supports it. A randomized pilot may be the next useful step when incremental response is unresolved.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Customer Data in an AI Workflow
bullets: Use only data authorized for the tool and task.
Minimize fields and use synthetic examples when they suffice.
Check where uploads, logs, and generated files are stored.
slides.notes: Public availability does not establish permission for every reuse. Pseudonymized histories can retain identifying patterns. A coding request should specify the permitted input and destination before any transfer.
slides.source: Course agent guide and ETHICS_AND_REGULATION.md, M1.

slides.title: Decision Discussion
bullets: Which customer receives the renewal offer?
What changes if every treated renewal receives a discount?
Which future variable would invalidate a Monday-morning forecast?
slides.notes: Under the stated synthetic inputs, B has higher incremental contribution. A discount paid to every renewing recipient reduces value by the treated renewal probability times the discount. A Wednesday service contact is unavailable for a Monday forecast.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.6, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

practice: Implement and assess order aggregation, then distinguish code errors from missing observations.
application: Write a coupon specification and identify the evidence needed to resolve its causal question.

title: Customer Data and Measurement
objectives: Construct customer metrics with explicit populations and denominators.
Separate missing observations, zeros, and unmatched keys.
Assess changing coverage in mHealth, McBroken, and earnings-call records.

slides.title: A Customer-Activity Decision
bullets: An mHealth manager wants to understand reduced recorded use.
The comparison follows the same eligible customers over time.
A missing record can reflect nonuse, incomplete observation, or data coverage.
slides.notes: Logging is an observable app behavior. Complete dietary consumption and health outcomes require additional measurement. A metric must state the population represented in each period.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: A Customer Table
bullets: Begin with the eligible-customer roster.
Aggregate events to the customer-period level.
Left join the summaries to the roster.
Fill zero only when absence has the defined meaning of no recorded event.
slides.notes: Starting from events omits customers with no observed events. Filling a missing nutrition measurement with zero changes its meaning. The roster and observation window establish the denominator.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Two Activity Measures
slides.intro: Let $D_i$ be observed logging days and $T$ the calendar days in a common window.
slides.interpretation: Each eligible customer receives equal weight, including customers with no recorded days.
slides.notes: The mean describes recorded use per available calendar day. Averaging only customers with positive D conditions on activity and can obscure declining use.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.10, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Conditional and Fixed Denominators
slides.caption: mHealth activity depends on who remains in the denominator.
slides.description: The figure contrasts a fixed eligible-user denominator with a denominator conditional on observed activity. The two series answer different questions.
slides.notes: The fixed cohort supports a comparison of changes in recorded use for the same customers. A conditional mean describes behavior among the customers still observed.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Repeated Totals
bullets: An item row can contain a copied daily total.
Five copies of 1,132.79 sum to 5,663.95.
The item-calorie sum on that example day is 1,132.7852.
slides.notes: The five-fold inflation follows from repeated measurement fields, not a nutritional mechanism. One daily value can be retained after checking agreement within the user-day. Small rounding differences do not justify ignoring larger discrepancies.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.8, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: Structural Errors and Review Flags
bullets: A duplicate daily key violates a one-row-per-day contract.
Equal item descriptions can represent repeated servings.
An extreme value warrants review under a stated rule.
slides.notes: Timestamp and meal identifiers are absent from the selected equality fields in the mHealth assessment. Dropping all equal records would impose a particular event definition. Preserve source values and add explicit flags.
slides.source: M1, Section 1.8.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md

slides.title: A Fixed Customer Denominator
slides.intro: Synthetic counts follow all four eligible customers.
slides.code:
days = {'A': 20, 'B': 10, 'C': 0, 'D': 0}
fixed = sum(days.values()) / (4 * 30)
active = [x for x in days.values() if x > 0]
conditional = sum(active) / (len(active) * 30)
assert round(fixed, 4) == 0.25
assert round(conditional, 4) == 0.50
slides.check: The fixed-roster rate is 25%. The active-user rate is 50%.
slides.notes: Both numbers use the same observed days. The denominator changes from 120 potential customer-days to 60. These are synthetic counts.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Cohorts and Customer Age
bullets: Group customers by a defined entry period.
Compare the same time since entry.
Mark later outcomes as unobserved when the horizon has not elapsed.
slides.notes: A recent cohort has no twelve-month outcome yet. Treating that cell as zero creates false attrition. The event defining entry must also remain stable across cohorts.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Retention Has a Triangular Support
slides.caption: Synthetic cohort structure. Blank cells have no elapsed follow-up.
slides.description: Older cohorts have more observable follow-up periods. The missing upper-age cells for recent cohorts are unobserved rather than zero retention.
slides.notes: Calendar time, tenure, and acquisition cohort are different dimensions. A comparison at fixed tenure avoids giving newer customers shorter opportunities to remain active.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: McBroken as a Measurement Case
bullets: The records describe ice-cream ordering availability.
A missing snapshot has an unknown status.
Restaurant coverage and status recognition can change over time.
slides.notes: Order unavailability can reflect conditions besides a verified mechanical breakdown. A parser must distinguish known available, known unavailable, and unrecognized states. The source assessment and data dictionary define those categories.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.16, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Coverage Changes the Percentage
slides.caption: McBroken comparisons preserve the observed-store denominator.
slides.description: The figure separates changing national coverage from comparisons on common observed support. Missing dates and unrecognized statuses do not become observed availability.
slides.notes: A change in the set of included restaurants can change the national share without a within-restaurant change. Common-support comparisons answer a narrower population question.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.16.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Identity Across Files
bullets: A restaurant address is a candidate key that requires checks.
Standardizing spelling can repair formatting differences.
Overaggressive matching can merge separate locations.
slides.notes: Track duplicates before and after normalization. Location identity and status measurement are separate tasks. A unique normalized string does not alone prove a unique physical establishment.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.16.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Earnings Calls: Missing Text and Zero Matches
bullets: A communications team wants a complete reading population.
One supplied call has 53 turns but zero recorded words.
Retain the call as unknown and preserve firms with no matches.
slides.notes: The roster contains 123 firms, of which 122 have supplied calls. Winmark has no supplied calls. The empty Dollar Tree call cannot establish absence of pricing language. Observed calls with no matches have a different status.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.19, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Selecting Matches Changes the Denominator
slides.caption: The same 112 positive calls, with two different populations.
slides.description: The full observed-call rate is 112/2,325 = 4.82%. Restricting the denominator to 445 calls with any core or broad match produces 25.17%.
slides.notes: Start with the call table and aggregate match occurrences before joining. The conditional rate among retrieved documents overstates the overall language frequency when presented without its selected denominator.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.19, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Coding Exercise: A Data Assessment
bullets: Construct a roster-first activity or call table.
Separate observed zeros, missing text, and unmatched keys.
Reconcile the full and match-selected call denominators.
slides.notes: Run assessment.py in ../03_Data_and_Code/Earnings_Calls. Verify 112/2,325 and 112/445; explain why Winmark has an unknown rate and observed no-match firms have zero rates. The customer aggregation exercise supplies a second application of the same roster-first principle.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.10, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: AI Review of a Parser
bullets: Supply the allowed statuses and a tiny labeled example.
Require an explicit unknown category for new statuses.
Compare parsed totals with an independently calculated source total.
slides.notes: A program that treats every unrecognized status as available can create artificial improvements. A counterexample containing a new status tests this failure directly.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.16.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: A Data Dictionary for Decisions
bullets: State the unit, key, timing, and units of each variable.
Record source versions and transformation rules.
Separate observed values, calculated quantities, and imposed assumptions.
slides.notes: A reader should be able to trace a plotted rate to its numerator and denominator without guessing the meaning of a field name.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Privacy and Collection Choices
bullets: Collect the fields needed for the stated decision.
Retain source permissions and deletion or retention conditions.
Check whether a linkage increases the risk of identifying a person.
slides.notes: Combining datasets can change what can be inferred even when each file omits names. Data minimization is part of the analytical design, and dataset-specific restrictions remain applicable.
slides.source: ETHICS_AND_REGULATION.md, M2.

slides.title: Measurement Discussion
bullets: Could recorded activity rise because low-activity users disappear?
Would deleting unmatched days change the target population?
What evidence would establish a mechanical failure?
slides.notes: Conditioning on observed users can raise activity among those remaining. An inner join changes the observed food-log population. A verified failure diagnosis requires information beyond online ordering availability.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.16, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

practice: Build roster-first summaries; assess missing text, zero-match calls, and selected denominators in the earnings-call case.
application: Compare restaurant coverage and conference-call disclosure using explicitly observed populations.

title: Visualization and Data Quality
objectives: Choose displays that preserve the intended comparison.
Explain composition reversals and uncertainty.
Use domain knowledge to define transparent sensitivity analyses.

slides.title: A Campaign Comparison
bullets: Campaign B converts more new and returning customers within each group.
Its aggregate conversion rate is lower.
The customer mix determines which comparison the aggregate makes.
slides.notes: The synthetic campaigns differ in the proportion of returning customers. The group rates and the aggregate can move in opposite directions without an arithmetic error.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Customer Mix Reverses the Ranking
slides.caption: Synthetic campaigns. Both within-group rates rise by one percentage point.
slides.description: Campaign A converts 9% of new and 80% of returning customers. B converts 10% and 81%. The observed rates are 44.5% and 33.7%, while a common 50:50 mix gives 44.5% and 45.5%.
slides.notes: Standardization holds group weights fixed. It supplies a common-population descriptive comparison. Causal interpretation would require evidence about assignment and comparability within groups.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: A Standardized Conversion Rate
slides.intro: Use common customer-group weights $w_g$ for each campaign $c$.
slides.interpretation: Changing the weights changes the population represented by the rate.
slides.notes: The same weights should apply to every campaign in the stated comparison. The group-specific rates can still reflect selection or other differences within groups.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Chart Choice Follows the Question
bullets: Aligned positions compare magnitudes.
Lines compare changes over ordered time.
Distributions reveal spread and concentration.
Paired displays preserve within-customer changes.
slides.notes: A mean alone can hide whether a change is widespread or concentrated in a small set of customers. Chart choice should follow the estimand and the decision.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: A Mean Decline Can Hide a Stable Median
slides.caption: mHealth comparison uses paired customers and a common observation window.
slides.description: The empirical distributions and paired changes distinguish the average change from the fraction of customers whose activity changed. A few large declines can move the mean.
slides.notes: Distribution spread describes variation among customer outcomes. Uncertainty about an average describes how precisely that average is estimated. They require different displays.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.14.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Uncertainty and Dependence
bullets: Repeated days for one customer share common influences.
Customer-level resampling preserves each customer history.
A confidence interval and a percentile range describe different objects.
slides.notes: An independent-day bootstrap treats days as separate sampling units and can understate uncertainty when observations within a user are correlated. A paired difference should also preserve the pairing.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.6.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Nutrition Knowledge and Measurement
bullets: A recorded food log can omit meals and portions.
Energy plausibility depends on the measurement instrument and physiology.
Age, body size, activity, and recording duration affect screening.
slides.notes: These records contain perturbed weights and undocumented source codes. The course example does not treat an undocumented gender code as validated physiological sex or a goal code as measured activity.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.11, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Sample Restrictions Change the Comparison
slides.caption: mHealth screening alternatives are explicit analysis choices.
slides.description: The figure compares sample definitions and their consequences. Structural checks, age restrictions, and imposed calorie ranges serve different purposes.
slides.notes: An imposed calorie range is a sensitivity analysis, not an individual diagnosis of adequate intake. Report the observations retained under each rule and compare the resulting estimands.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.11, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Access Changes the Evidence Sample
slides.caption: November 5, 2026 snapshot. Counts refer to DOI records and retrieved versions.
slides.description: The 886-record census becomes 824 eligible records, 103 retrieved versions, and 48 papers coded with potential agency concerns. Access and coding change the denominator.
slides.notes: The primary mechanism sample includes 47 potential-dual-use reviews and one reported choice concern. Abstract-only papers selected for teaching enter a separate sensitivity sample. Unreviewed papers retain missing codes. The complete coverage calculation appears in M2 Section 2.20.
slides.source: ../01_Resources/13_Consumer_Agency_and_Recent_Research/README.md

slides.title: Selected Findings at a Fixed Date
slides.caption: Fifty selected claims, twenty models, and a September 2026 endpoint.
slides.notes: The released data contain 1,000 model-claim pairs, with eight flagged unreliable comparisons. These categories describe the selected claims under the authors' rules. An expired category allows a residual effect and exceptions among individual models. The point-estimate threshold is not the whole classification rule.
slides.source: Queen and Zou (2026). https://zou-group.github.io/llm-claims-shelf-life/ M2 §2.21. ../01_Resources/14_LLM_Evidence_and_Revalidation/README.md

slides.title: Follow-up Changes the Denominator
slides.caption: All fifty claims contribute follow-up; 28 remain right-censored.
slides.description: Kaplan-Meier point estimates give 4.0%, 16.0%, and 38.9% expired at six, twelve, and twenty-four months. Published estimated dates are treated as fixed.
slides.notes: The 15.75-month mean conditions on the 22 expired claims. It is not an expected lifetime for all findings. The displayed calculation retains the unexpired claims until the observation endpoint. Interval-based and model-count dates are treated as the authors' point estimates; their uncertainty is not propagated.
slides.source: Queen and Zou (2026), released fitted dates; original course calculation. ../01_Resources/14_LLM_Evidence_and_Revalidation/README.md

slides.title: Energy-Plausibility Screens
bullets: An intake-to-requirement comparison needs defined inputs.
Unobserved physiological inputs remain missing.
A hypothetical Goldberg calculation teaches the method separately from the logs.
slides.notes: The Goldberg example in the notes is an explicitly hypothetical scenario. Its inputs should not be silently imputed from undocumented codes. Screening validity depends on the instrument and population.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.11.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Interactive Comparisons
bullets: Keep comparable panels on common scales.
Display the eligible population and current selection.
Preserve customers with no recorded days when the estimand includes them.
slides.notes: Changing a slider can change the population, the denominator, and the axis range simultaneously. These changes should remain visible and should be checked against an aggregate table.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.15, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: A Composition Check
slides.intro: Synthetic within-group rates are 9%, 80%, 10%, and 81%.
slides.code:
rates_a = [0.09, 0.80]
rates_b = [0.10, 0.81]
common_a = sum(rates_a) / 2
common_b = sum(rates_b) / 2
observed_b = (2 * rates_b[0] + rates_b[1]) / 3
assert round(common_b - common_a, 2) == 0.01
slides.check: B improves by one point under common weights despite its lower observed aggregate.
slides.notes: The observed B mix assigns two-thirds of its customers to the new-customer group. This calculation is descriptive and uses imposed rates.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Coding Exercise: A Chart Assessment
bullets: Generate a rate chart from a verified aggregate table.
Alter the axis range, cohort filter, and denominator one at a time.
Explain which changes alter the substantive comparison.
slides.notes: The small example runs with ../03_Data_and_Code/Lecture_Examples/session_examples.py S03. The complete mHealth visualization program and interactive chart provide the real-data extension. Verify values separately from rendered readability.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: A Public-Signal Measurement Problem
bullets: A product can acquire a new page title while demand stays unchanged.
A single-title series then misses part of its recorded attention.
Coverage, redirects, and missing dates require an assessment.
slides.notes: Pageviews measure attention to selected pages. They do not directly measure paid demand or unique customers. Alias aggregation also needs checks for duplicate coverage.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.17, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Title Changes and Apparent Declines
slides.caption: The supplied public pageview capture uses observed title histories.
slides.description: A single-title view and an alias-aware view differ when the product identity moves across titles. The display retains the distinction between missing coverage and a measured zero.
slides.notes: The GenAI measurement program validates date and title coverage before calculating a product series. Its saved tables are the values behind the plotted comparison.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.17.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Evidence in a Management Presentation
bullets: State the decision and supported result.
Show the comparison, units, and denominator.
Keep the qualification that could change the action beside the claim.
slides.notes: An executive summary can be concise while retaining consequential uncertainty. A useful chart title states the population and comparison rather than a causal claim unsupported by the design.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.7, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

slides.title: Honest Comparisons
bullets: Keep denominators and scales visible.
Preserve missing outcomes and relevant subgroup variation.
Avoid presenting a filtered descriptive pattern as a general causal effect.
slides.notes: A technically correct chart can still communicate a stronger claim than the evidence supports. The reader's likely interpretation matters when selecting a title and comparison.
slides.source: ETHICS_AND_REGULATION.md, M2-M3.

slides.title: Visualization Discussion
bullets: Which customers receive weight in the chart?
Could sample restrictions reverse the recommendation?
What does the uncertainty interval include?
slides.notes: The answers should identify whether the unit is an event, a day, or a customer. Sensitivity to inclusion rules can indicate that the decision depends on a narrower population than the headline suggests.
slides.source: M2, Section 2.8, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md

practice: Assess chart values, paired changes, scales, and denominator controls.
application: Compare nutrition screens and public-page identity changes without changing the measurement claim.

title: Regression and Marketing Interpretation
objectives: Interpret coefficients with units and conditioning.
Diagnose omitted variables, interactions, and dependence.
Reproduce an association while preserving its time and sample definitions.

slides.title: Competitors and Store Sales
bullets: Stores in markets with more competitors can have higher sales.
Demand attracts firms and also raises sales.
The managerial question concerns the effect of an additional competitor.
slides.notes: A positive cross-market association can combine the negative competitive effect with the selection of firms into high-demand markets. The mechanism determines which comparison is informative.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: A Conditional Mean
slides.intro: Relate store sales to observed marketing conditions.
slides.interpretation: The coefficient on $X_i$ describes its linear association holding included $Z_i$ fixed.
slides.notes: The outcome and regressors require explicit units and timing. A conditional association becomes a causal parameter only under the assumptions supplied by the design and model.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Ordinary Least Squares
bullets: OLS chooses coefficients to minimize squared residuals.
A residual is observed sales minus fitted sales.
The model summarizes the comparison supplied by the data.
slides.notes: The fitted residuals sum to zero when an intercept is included and the usual OLS solution exists. This algebraic property does not establish independence between treatment and unobserved demand.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Omitted Demand Reverses the Sign
slides.caption: Synthetic markets hold the underlying competitive mechanism fixed.
slides.description: Within-demand comparisons show a different relationship from the pooled trend because high-demand markets attract more competitors.
slides.notes: Market demand affects both entry and sales. Controlling for a valid measure of demand can change the regression coefficient by changing which observations are compared.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Omitted-Variable Bias
slides.intro: Suppose demand $Z$ affects sales and is omitted from a regression on $X$.
slides.interpretation: The omitted association can offset or reverse the coefficient of interest.
slides.notes: This expression is the population linear-projection result under the stated model and orthogonality conditions. Its sign depends on both the effect of Z and its association with X.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Price and Sales Units
bullets: A level coefficient is sales units per dollar.
A log-log price coefficient is an elasticity under the model.
The exact change for a log outcome uses an exponential transformation.
slides.notes: A coefficient on a binary regressor in a log-outcome model implies a multiplicative change of exp(beta)-1 under the relevant conditional interpretation. A percentage-point change in a probability is a different unit.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Interactions
slides.intro: Allow a message association to vary with account tenure $T$.
slides.interpretation: The message comparison at tenure $T$ is $\beta_1+\beta_3T$.
slides.notes: The main message coefficient applies at tenure zero under this parameterization. Centering tenure changes that reference point while leaving fitted values unchanged.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: A Comparison Changes With Tenure
slides.caption: Synthetic message-response model. Tenure determines the conditional comparison.
slides.description: The interaction changes the slope of the message comparison across customer tenure. A single main coefficient describes only the chosen reference tenure.
slides.notes: The marginal comparison should be reported at meaningful tenures within the observed support. A crossing outside the sample range is an extrapolation.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Uncertainty and Practical Importance
bullets: Report effect size in managerial units.
Cluster at the unit that shares outcome disturbances or assignment.
Compare the interval with a decision-relevant magnitude.
slides.notes: A small p-value does not measure the size of an effect. A wide interval containing zero can also contain large economically consequential effects. The appropriate sampling unit depends on the design.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.6, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Panel Comparisons
bullets: Customer effects absorb stable customer characteristics.
Time effects absorb shocks shared within a period.
Time-varying confounding can remain.
slides.notes: Fixed effects change the variation used for estimation. Stable preferences can be absorbed, while unobserved events that change both behavior and outcomes can still confound the within-customer association.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.7, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: mHealth: The Next Calendar Day
bullets: Relate recorded category breadth to next-day recorded calories.
Match exact adjacent calendar dates.
State the included users, days, and calorie restrictions.
slides.notes: The next observed row can be several days later. Calling it next-day intake would change the time horizon. The food logs identify recorded quantities, and the regression remains an association.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.10, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Screening and the Estimated Association
slides.caption: mHealth estimates retain the stated outcome timing and sample restrictions.
slides.description: The figure compares the association under the base sample and an imposed calorie-range restriction. The sample rule changes the observed support.
slides.notes: A robustness comparison should report which rows change and whether the estimand remains comparable. The range restriction is an imposed screen, not proof that excluded records are incorrect.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.10, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: A Hand-Checkable Regression
slides.intro: Synthetic sales follow a linear relationship.
slides.code:
x = [1, 2, 3, 4]
y = [3, 5, 7, 9]
mx, my = sum(x) / 4, sum(y) / 4
b = sum((a-mx)*(v-my) for a,v in zip(x,y))
b /= sum((a-mx)**2 for a in x)
a = my - b * mx
assert (a, b) == (1.0, 2.0)
slides.check: The intercept is 1 and the slope is 2 sales units per unit of x.
slides.notes: This example checks the covariance-over-variance calculation. Perfect fit is imposed by construction and is not an empirical finding about marketing behavior.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Coding Exercise: Regression Checks
bullets: Generate a model after defining the outcome and information set.
Verify the coefficient units and one fitted value manually.
Compare pooled and customer-effect specifications.
Inspect residuals, outliers, and sample changes.
slides.notes: Run the small OLS case in ../03_Data_and_Code/Lecture_Examples/session_examples.py S04. The mHealth m03.py program supplies the full real-data calculation, including exact-date pairing and clustered inference.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.8, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Prices Respond to Demand
bullets: Managers can raise prices when demand is unusually strong.
An observed price-sales regression can mix demand and pricing choices.
An instrument needs relevance and a defensible exclusion restriction.
slides.notes: The course price simulation sets the true elasticity and the source of price endogeneity explicitly. A cost shifter is useful as an instrument only when its other paths to demand can be ruled out under the maintained setting.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.12, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

slides.title: Evidence for an Advertised Claim
bullets: A claim that a product cuts costs needs a suitable comparison.
An association can reflect selection and omitted demand.
The evidence should support the express and implied claim before publication.
slides.notes: The FTC advertising-substantiation policy requires a reasonable basis for objective claims before dissemination. The necessary support depends on the claim and consequences. This does not turn every regression into an advertising substantiation study.
slides.source: FTC Policy Statement Regarding Advertising Substantiation. https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/ftc-policy-statement-regarding-advertising-substantiation

slides.title: Regression Discussion
bullets: Which comparison supports the coefficient?
What variable could reverse its interpretation?
Would the recommended action change across the reported interval?
slides.notes: A useful interpretation identifies the sample, units, conditioning, and causal scope before a recommendation. The source of variation matters as much as the regression command.
slides.source: M3, Section 3.8, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M03_Regression.md

practice: Reproduce OLS and assess exact-day matching, specification, and uncertainty.
application: Interpret a price coefficient when the manager observes demand before setting price.

title: Conjoint and Product Design
objectives: Design choice tasks that identify attribute tradeoffs.
Compute logit probabilities and willingness to pay.
Separate new-product share from incremental category demand.

slides.title: Customers Compare Product Bundles
slides.description: Customers compare distinct tea, fruit, and delivery offerings in a riverside market. The scene represents choice among available product bundles.
slides.notes: Product design changes a choice set. Sales of a new bundle can replace purchases of existing bundles or attract customers who previously chose the outside option.
slides.source: Original conceptual illustration. 05_Slides/assets/PROVENANCE.md.

slides.title: A Subscription-Bundle Decision
bullets: A firm can change quality, delivery, and monthly price.
Customers must trade off feasible attribute combinations.
The choice set includes the option to buy nothing.
slides.notes: A forced choice among paid plans estimates conditional preference. It supplies no direct category-participation margin when customers cannot opt out.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Choice-Task Design
bullets: Vary price independently of features where feasible.
Use realistic combinations and clear descriptions.
Retain respondent identity across repeated tasks.
slides.notes: Perfect correlation between price and quality prevents their separate interpretation. Repeated answers from one person are dependent, affecting estimation and validation.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Utility and Price
slides.intro: Systematic utility combines product features and price.
slides.interpretation: Utility has an arbitrary scale. Price is measured in dollars per billing period.
slides.notes: Coefficients describe tradeoffs within the specified design. Alternative-specific constants and preference heterogeneity can change the appropriate model.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Logit Choice Probabilities
slides.intro: Normalize probabilities over the alternatives available to customer $i$.
slides.interpretation: The denominator includes the outside option and every available product.
slides.notes: Probabilities sum to one within each choice set. The multinomial logit model imposes proportional substitution among alternatives. That restriction requires assessment in the category.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Willingness to Pay
slides.intro: Under linear price utility, equate a feature gain with a price increase.
slides.interpretation: If $\beta_f=1.2$ and $\beta_p=-0.1$ per dollar, the tradeoff is 12 dollars.
slides.notes: A near-zero price coefficient makes the ratio unstable. WTP is conditional on the model, design range, and respondent population. It is not a direct forecast of revenue.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Two Bundles and an Outside Option
slides.caption: Synthetic inputs: quality coefficient 1.2 and price coefficient -0.1.
slides.notes: The outside utility is normalized to zero. Prices and coefficients determine the utilities. The example holds the potential-customer population fixed.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: A Launch Redistributes Existing Sales
slides.caption: Synthetic logit model. New bundle C has A's modeled attributes.
slides.description: C obtains about 30.6% share, while category participation rises by about 11.0 percentage points. Existing bundles lose share.
slides.notes: The difference between C share and incremental category demand is substitution from existing products. The logit specification makes C draw proportionally from all existing alternatives.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Incremental Contribution
bullets: Attach contribution margins to each simulated purchase.
Compare the full product portfolio before and after launch.
Deduct development and operating costs separately.
slides.notes: Under the supplied margins of 4 dollars for A and C and 3 for B, expected contribution per potential customer rises from about 2.36 to 2.86 dollars before fixed costs. These are model-based values under imposed inputs.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: A Probability Check
slides.intro: Calculate the synthetic baseline shares.
slides.check: A has about 44.1% share, B 19.8%, and the outside option 36.1%.
slides.notes: For very large utilities, subtracting the maximum utility before exponentiation improves numerical stability without changing probabilities.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Substitution Assumptions
bullets: A close copy can draw mostly from its nearest competitor.
Basic logit instead preserves relative odds among existing alternatives.
Holdout choice tasks can reveal systematic substitution errors.
slides.notes: Nested and mixed logit models relax substitution patterns under additional structure. More flexible models still need suitable choice variation and validation.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Coding Exercise: A Product Launch
bullets: Add C to the synthetic profile table.
Calculate portfolio share and contribution before and after launch.
Compare C's share with the change in category participation.
Check a case with no outside option.
slides.notes: Use ../03_Data_and_Code/Lecture_Examples/session_examples.py S05. With no outside option, purchase incidence is one by construction. That change should be visible in the program and interpretation.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.10, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Validation and Market Transfer
bullets: Hold out respondents or tasks according to the intended use.
Check coding, price units, and probabilities.
Relate stated preference to awareness, distribution, and availability.
slides.notes: A survey share is conditional on the experiment. Real demand also depends on who sees the offering and whether they can buy it. The demand forecast needs an explicit transfer assumption.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: mHealth Product Economics
bullets: Food logs reveal recorded use and category histories.
A paid-plan choice model needs additional price and preference evidence.
Financial scenarios can state the missing inputs explicitly.
slides.notes: The lecture notes use an imposed paid-plan logit example separately from observed logs. Behavioral logging segments do not establish willingness to pay or paid subscription retention.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.11, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: AI-Assisted Conjoint Analysis
bullets: Provide the choice-set identifier and the selected alternative.
Require probabilities to sum to one within each task.
Preserve respondent groups in validation.
Request a portfolio comparison with explicit margins.
slides.notes: A code generator may accidentally normalize probabilities over the full dataset or treat repeated tasks as independent respondents. Small constructed tasks expose those errors.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.10, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Customer Alternatives and AI Pricing
bullets: Customer value depends on the offered outcome and implementation effort.
Better tools can make internal analysis a stronger alternative.
Lower seller costs and lower willingness to pay can occur together.
slides.notes: Under a quasilinear comparison, the buyer price ceiling is delivered value minus buyer burden and outside-option utility. Use a common customer and horizon. Product design can reduce integration and verification effort, while competitive improvements raise the value of the alternative. The conditional numerical comparison appears in Session 14 and M8 §8.17.
slides.source: Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes, M4 §4.16.

slides.title: Price Presentation and Customer Understanding
bullets: A base price and a mandatory fee determine the total paid.
A stated-choice task can reveal different responses to equivalent totals.
The feasible pricing design depends on the applicable rule and industry.
slides.notes: The FTC's fee rule addresses live-event tickets and short-term lodging. Its scope should remain explicit. A response difference to fee framing does not itself authorize a particular presentation.
slides.source: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees FAQ. https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/rule-unfair-or-deceptive-fees-frequently-asked-questions

slides.title: Product-Design Discussion
bullets: How much of C's demand comes from existing products?
Which design change would identify the price tradeoff?
What evidence could change the launch recommendation?
slides.notes: The recommendation depends on substitution, incremental contribution, and costs. An appealing new-product share can coexist with little category expansion.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

practice: Calculate choice probabilities and assess the role of a stronger customer alternative.
application: Compare product value, implementation burden, substitution, and the outside option.

title: Segmentation and Customer Lifetime Value
objectives: Define similarity using economically meaningful customer features.
Evaluate segment stability and future outcomes.
Calculate lifetime value with consistent timing and distinguish retention concepts.

slides.title: A Retention-Support Decision
bullets: A service team can support only some customers.
High baseline value and responsiveness to support are separate quantities.
Segments should correspond to feasible service decisions.
slides.notes: A segment with high predicted value may have little incremental response to outreach. The support decision needs the change in future contribution caused by the action, net of its costs.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.9, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Customer Features at a Common Date
bullets: Recency is time since the last eligible event.
Frequency counts events in a fixed window.
Monetary value uses sales or contribution over that window.
slides.notes: Customers with unequal exposure histories can appear different because of observation time. The feature definition must specify eligibility and whether returns affect sales or transaction counts.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: K-Means and Similarity
slides.intro: Choose $K$ centers for transformed customer features $z_i$.
slides.interpretation: Scaling the features changes the distance and can change the segments.
slides.notes: K-means minimizes within-cluster squared Euclidean distance. A standardized feature receives a different implicit weight from the raw variable. The transformation is a substantive choice.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Units Change the Nearest Customer
slides.caption: Synthetic customers have unchanged spending and frequency records.
slides.description: Changing spending from dollars to hundreds of dollars reverses which customer is nearest to A. Frequency then receives more relative weight.
slides.notes: Raw distances compare A=(100,1), B=(110,9), and C=(200,1). The example changes only the spending scale. The preferred business representation depends on the service decision.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Evaluating a Segmentation
bullets: Inspect segment size, profile, and actionable differences.
Compare stability across seeds, samples, and periods.
Evaluate outcomes that did not mechanically define the clusters.
slides.notes: Within-cluster dispersion declines as K rises. A high-spending cluster will have high spending by construction when spending is an input. Later outcomes provide a more informative descriptive check.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.6, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Similarity of Positive Mechanisms
slides.intro: For each paper, collect the mechanisms coded as present in a set $A_i$.
slides.interpretation: Jaccard distance ignores shared absences. Average linkage compares these distances.
slides.notes: The primary sample is 48 retrieved papers with potential dual use or a reported choice concern. Twelve binary codes include social cues, emotion, disclosure, defaults, and exit friction. A zero code means the mechanism was not coded from reviewed evidence. Missing reviews are excluded. See M4 Section 4.17 for the complete program.
slides.source: ../03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature/README.md

slides.title: Social Influence is the Largest Cluster
slides.caption: 48 retrieved potential-risk reviews. Four clusters selected from K=2 through K=8.
slides.description: Social influence contains 19 papers, emotion and identity 15, disclosure/framing/defaults eight, and attention/search/control six. The horizontal scale runs from zero to the full sample of 48.
slides.notes: The largest cluster contains 39.6% of the sample. Emotion/identity is the most common overlapping feature at 21 of 48, so feature and cluster rankings differ. Almost all papers in this analysis are coded for inferred dual use. Counts do not measure market prevalence or author intent.
slides.source: ../03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature/README.md

slides.title: Reproduce the Mechanism Grouping
slides.intro: Run from the Consumer_Agency_Literature folder after installing its requirements.
slides.code:
import pandas as pd
from cluster import FEATURES, select_sample, partition
df = pd.read_csv("coded_papers.csv")
sample = select_sample(df, "downloaded_risk")
labels, distances = partition(sample[FEATURES].to_numpy(), 4)
assert len(sample) == 48
slides.check: The complete script compares K values, exports profiles, and refits sensitivity samples.
slides.notes: The short snippet reproduces the selected four-cluster partition. The full cluster.py program in M4 Section 4.17 selects K using silhouette scores and checks aggregate counts. Stable paper identifiers preserve traceability to original summaries.
slides.source: ../03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature/README.md

slides.title: The Coding Changes the Conclusion
bullets: Median subsample agreement: adjusted Rand index 0.794.
Changing one feature per paper lowers median agreement to 0.250.
The broader abstract-based sample selects eight clusters.
slides.notes: Subsamples contain 80% of the primary papers and hold K=4 fixed across 200 repetitions. One-bit changes are an imposed sensitivity exercise, retaining a positive feature per paper. These are conditional stability results, not confidence intervals for population harm. The broader 84-paper risk sample is purposefully selected and chooses the upper K boundary.
slides.source: ../03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature/README.md

slides.title: mHealth Segments Use Earlier Histories
slides.caption: Eligible users have at least 30 observed days before July 1.
slides.description: Earlier logging frequency and recorded breadth distinguish clusters. Later logging does not enter the clustering inputs.
slides.notes: The representation uses first-half logging fraction, mean category breadth, and mean calorie-share variety. K=3 is imposed for the comparison. The scaler and centers use only the earlier window.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.11, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Later Logging by Earlier Segment
slides.caption: mHealth denominators use 182 earlier and 184 later calendar days.
slides.notes: Later absence contributes zero observed days for eligible users. The figures describe persistence in recorded activity. They are not contractual retention rates or effects of a service intervention.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.11, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Lifetime Value and Payment Timing
slides.intro: Value future contribution conditional on remaining active.
slides.interpretation: The period for margin $m_t$, discounting $d$, and retention must agree.
slides.notes: The acquisition cost a occurs at time zero. This convention excludes immediate contribution. If a current-period contribution is included, it must be added explicitly.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.7, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: A Stationary Subscription
slides.intro: Suppose monthly retention is $r$ and monthly contribution is $m$.
slides.notes: The formula assumes constant retention and conditional margin and an infinite horizon, with the first payment one month later. It follows from a convergent geometric series.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.7, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Retention Has Nonlinear Value
slides.caption: Synthetic stationary model. Monthly margin, discounting, and acquisition cost stay fixed.
slides.description: CLV rises increasingly rapidly with retention. Increasing monthly retention from 0.80 to 0.90 raises value from about 178.57 to 440.91 dollars.
slides.notes: The high-retention region places more weight on distant contributions. Uncertainty about the persistence of retention and margins can dominate the valuation.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.7, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: A Finite-Sum Check
slides.intro: Compare the closed form with 2,000 future monthly payments.
slides.code:
m, r, d, a = 60, 0.8, 0.01, 50
closed = m * r / (1 + d - r) - a
finite = sum(m * r**t / (1+d)**t
             for t in range(1, 2001)) - a
assert abs(closed - finite) < 1e-8
slides.notes: Matching the two expressions checks the payment convention and arithmetic. It does not establish constant retention as a valid model of a real relationship.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.7, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Cancellation and a Logging Gap
bullets: A subscription may record cancellation directly.
A 30-day logging gap is an operational activity event.
Observation can end before a defined event occurs.
slides.notes: Right censoring preserves the distinction between no observed event by the end of follow-up and an event at the last observation. A logging gap is not proof of permanent departure or paid cancellation.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.13, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: The Event Definition Changes Survival
slides.caption: mHealth time-to-gap analysis uses a stated gap definition and observation horizon.
slides.description: Survival tracks time until a defined logging gap. The risk set and right censoring determine which histories contribute at each time.
slides.notes: Changing the gap length changes the event being measured. Survival of recorded activity should remain separate from contractual renewal in financial calculations.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.13, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Endpoint and Continuous Retention
bullets: Endpoint retention allows customers to leave and return.
Continuous retention requires uninterrupted presence.
Acquisition can include first entry, return, or switching.
slides.notes: A starting-provider cohort is fixed at the initial period. The same-provider, other-provider-only, and no-paid-provider states distinguish platform retention from category participation. Multiple providers require explicit overlap handling.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Coding Exercise: Segments and Value
bullets: Fit feature scaling and segments on an earlier period.
Describe a later period without refitting the groups.
Vary assumed paid retention in a separate CLV calculation.
slides.notes: The small CLV calculation is ../03_Data_and_Code/Lecture_Examples/session_examples.py S06. The real mHealth m04.py example and GenAI cohort program keep behavioral measurements separate from imposed financial inputs.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.11, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: Retention and Effective Cancellation
bullets: High paid retention can reflect satisfaction or difficulty leaving.
Measure cancellation completion and unwanted subsequent charges.
Evaluate customer value alongside the seller's lifetime-value objective.
slides.notes: A customer who prefers cancellation can remain subscribed because of friction. The consumer-value comparison requires independent evidence about that preference and the available procedure.
slides.source: M8, Section 8.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M08_Current_Topics_and_Integrated_Decisions.md

slides.title: Retention Discussion
bullets: What action differs across the proposed segments?
Does a customer's absence represent churn or censoring?
Which retention assumption changes the support decision?
slides.notes: A useful recommendation identifies the response to intervention as well as baseline value. Cluster membership alone does not establish the effectiveness of differentiated support.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.9, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md
