title: Text, Social Media, and Networks
objectives: Define a text construct and evaluate labels on the deployment population.
Distinguish prevalence, text exposure, retrieval, and substantive interpretation.
Explain network reach and brokerage without inferring influence from correlation.

slides.title: A Customer-Service Decision
bullets: A retailer wants to detect delivery complaints quickly.
The document may be a review, sentence, or service conversation.
The action is a review queue with limited staff capacity.
slides.notes: The unit and label definition determine the evaluation. A negative review can concern price or quality rather than delivery. A classifier needs a construct that matches the service action.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Text Preparation
bullets: Keep negation and domain-specific terms when they affect meaning.
Document language, duplicates, and boilerplate.
Fit the vocabulary on training documents.
slides.notes: Removing the word not can reverse a sentiment label. Duplicate descriptions across train and test can produce a favorable score for a task requiring generalization to new text.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: TF-IDF Representation
slides.intro: Weight a term by frequency in a document and rarity across documents.
slides.interpretation: Tokenization, smoothing, and normalization are implementation choices that need a record.
slides.notes: Different packages use different conventions. A rare word can be predictive without being substantively important. The vocabulary and IDF values must be learned from the training corpus.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Embeddings and Similarity
bullets: Embeddings place text in a numerical representation.
Nearby descriptions may share meaning or usage.
A useful similarity measure still requires domain validation.
slides.notes: A semantic model can confuse closely related foods that have distinct nutritional properties. A cosine score is a representation-based similarity, not a probability of label correctness.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Labels, Sentiment, and Topics
bullets: Sentiment measures an evaluative construct.
Aspect labels distinguish the object of a complaint.
Topics summarize recurring term patterns under a model.
slides.notes: A high-weight topic term does not establish a causal driver of satisfaction. Topic names are interpretations that should be checked against representative documents.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Rare Complaints Lower Precision
slides.caption: Synthetic classifier. Sensitivity is 80% and specificity is 90%.
slides.description: At 1% prevalence, only about 7.5% of flagged reviews are true complaints. At 20% prevalence, precision rises to 66.7%.
slides.notes: The classifier has unchanged conditional error rates. The changing base rate alters the composition of the flagged group and therefore the workload of human reviewers.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Precision Depends on Prevalence
slides.intro: Let $\pi$ be complaint prevalence, $s$ sensitivity, and $c$ specificity.
slides.interpretation: False positives can dominate a queue when the target condition is rare.
slides.notes: The formula applies to the specified population and classifier. Prevalence should come from an appropriate deployment sample rather than an artificially balanced training set.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Expected Queue Composition
slides.intro: In 10,000 synthetic reviews, complaint prevalence is 1%.
slides.code:
n, prevalence = 10000, 0.01
sensitivity, specificity = 0.8, 0.9
tp = n * prevalence * sensitivity
fp = n * (1-prevalence) * (1-specificity)
precision = tp / (tp + fp)
assert round(precision, 4) == 0.0748
slides.check: The expected queue contains 80 true complaints and 990 false positives.
slides.notes: These are expected counts under the imposed rates. Actual counts vary. Capacity planning should consider the queue size as well as sensitivity.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Human and LLM Annotation
bullets: Write a label definition with difficult boundary examples.
Measure agreement and adjudicate disagreements.
Assess a held-out sample with human labels.
Record the model, prompt, and response format.
slides.notes: Agreement measures consistency, not necessarily construct validity. When a model labels the data used to evaluate itself, the resulting score can reproduce its own labeling choices. A sponsor-framing comparison can hold the same proposal fixed while varying whether the sponsor likes it. Evaluate factual criticism separately from approval. This is a proposed exercise motivated by Sharma et al.; no course model responses have been collected.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.6, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md Sharma et al. (2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13548v4. M5 §5.18.

slides.title: Agency Labels Need Supporting Evidence
bullets: Extract the outcome, mechanism, study design, and supporting passage.
Separate reported choice concerns from inferred possible misuse.
Retain uncertain cases and compare independent coding.
slides.notes: Consumer agency concerns understanding, choice, action, and revision or exit. Persuasion alone does not establish impairment. The current literature codes are preliminary AI-assisted annotations without independent human adjudication. Immersive Service supplies qualitative agency evidence; Nudging App Adoption supplies evidence about choice presentation whose misuse requires an additional inference. See M5 Section 5.16.
slides.source: ../03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature/README.md

slides.title: mHealth Food Descriptions
bullets: Descriptions can recur across many users and dates.
A repeated-description split evaluates familiar language.
A held-out-description split tests generalization to new language.
slides.notes: The source category is an imperfect label. The same normalized description can have multiple source labels. Evaluation should retain that ambiguity rather than assume a single validated nutrition category.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.10, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Familiar and New Text Are Different Tests
slides.caption: mHealth text classification uses the stated training and evaluation splits.
slides.description: The comparison separates repeated descriptions from new descriptions and identifies source-label ambiguity. Performance depends on the deployment question.
slides.notes: A random event split can place an identical description in both training and test. That may be useful for repeated lookup but overstate performance on new descriptions.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.10, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Topic Shares Need a Denominator
slides.caption: mHealth topic summaries compare documents, entries, and users under defined weights.
slides.description: A topic common in repeated entries can look less prevalent when distinct descriptions or equally weighted users form the denominator.
slides.notes: Long documents and repeated records can dominate term-weighted summaries. A business question about the fraction of affected customers needs a customer denominator.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.12, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Which Pricing Statements Deserve Review?
bullets: A retailer reviews competitors' public pricing communication.
A keyword occurrence supplies a reading lead.
Define the priced object, timing, and evidence before interpreting adoption.
slides.notes: The supplied corpus includes core terms for pricing methods and shelf-label infrastructure. Among observed calls, core-call rates are 2.90% in retail, 2.02% in restaurants, and 10.49% in the selected comparison group. These are call-weighted disclosure rates.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Speaking Time Changes the Comparison
slides.caption: Observed calls; heuristic roles. Management includes prepared remarks and Q&A.
slides.description: Management has 127 core occurrences in 16,685,338 words, versus analysts' 23 in 2,761,999 words. Rates are 0.076 and 0.083 per 10,000 words.
slides.notes: Raw counts rank management higher, whereas exposure-adjusted intensity is slightly higher for analysts. This is a descriptive arithmetic comparison, with different formats and heuristic labels. Restricting both counts and words to detected-Q&A calls gives rates of 0.072 and 0.083.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Same Vocabulary, Different Evidence
bullets: Amazon: current price information; Eventbrite: advertising cost per click.
Wendy's: planned tests; Kroger: shelf-label infrastructure.
A claim about use still requires evidence on implementation and outcomes.
slides.notes: Seven purposeful, source-linked paraphrases are provided in interpretation_cases.csv. They are examples of construct distinctions, not a representative precision sample. Delta's January 2025 question recorded as management/prepared also motivates reviewing heuristic speaker boundaries.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Match Counts and Words to the Same Calls
slides.intro: From the Earnings_Calls folder, compare the verified metadata.
slides.code:
from assessment import load_checked
from disclosure import role_rates
calls, mentions, _, _ = load_checked()
rates = role_rates(calls, mentions, require_qa=True)
assert rates.calls.eq(2240).all()
print(rates[['role', 'core_matches', 'per_10000_words']])
slides.check: Excluding a call removes both its occurrences and its words.
slides.notes: Run disclosure.py for group, quarterly, and role tables. The counterexample test includes one excluded call with many words; dropping only its matches would change the rate incorrectly.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Evaluate Retrieval and Interpretation Separately
bullets: A denial and a future intention can match the same phrase.
Relevant paraphrases can escape the dictionary.
Validate held-out firms or later calls with independently labeled hits and misses.
slides.notes: Run construct_checks.py for eight synthetic sentences. A purposeful case set cannot estimate corpus precision or recall. Probability sampling and appropriate weights are needed for population metrics. No external model or labeling API was run for the supplied course example.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Prompt Revision Uses Evaluation Evidence
bullets: A passage used to revise a prompt becomes development material.
Keep passages from one call together when constructing a split.
Freeze the prompt and reference-label procedure before fresh evaluation.
slides.notes: A test on new firms addresses a different deployment population from a test on later calls from familiar firms. Repeated passages are not independent firm-level replications. Evaluate a competent dictionary baseline with the same eligible evidence. Once final labels guide a revision, a later confirmation needs new evidence or a justified adaptive-evaluation design.
slides.source: Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes, M5 §5.15.

slides.title: Generator and Judge Changes
slides.caption: Identical saved outputs are scored by both judges. All scores are stipulated.
slides.description: Old-judge scores are 60 and 62; new-judge scores are 75 and 77. The generator gain is two points within either judge, while the diagonal comparison is seventeen.
slides.notes: A stable judge supplies a common comparison but still requires validation. Position, verbosity, and self-preference can affect evaluation. For earnings-call summaries, independently check factual support, speaker role, and whether a statement concerns a plan or an implemented action. Preserve inconsistent judgments.
slides.source: M5 §5.18. Zheng et al. (2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685; Panickssery et al. (2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13076

slides.title: Network Objects
bullets: Nodes identify customers or accounts.
Edges represent a defined relationship in a time window.
Degree counts links, while brokerage concerns paths between groups.
slides.notes: An edge could mean following, messaging, purchasing together, or co-occurrence. Those meanings are not interchangeable. The network boundary determines which relationships are visible.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.7, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Few Links Can Connect Separate Groups
slides.caption: Synthetic undirected network. R has only two links.
slides.description: R connects two otherwise separate four-person groups. Its low degree coexists with a central position on paths between the groups.
slides.notes: Brokerage can matter for reach even when a node has few direct neighbors. Observed network structure does not by itself establish the effect of targeting that person.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.7, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: University Affiliations Create a Research Network
bullets: 745 papers identify 424 higher-education institutions.
Split one unit of link weight across each paper's university pairs.
Shared-paper links can also arise from a single author's dual affiliation.
slides.notes: The eligible census has 824 papers; 79 lack identified education affiliations. Work-specific metadata is used rather than current author profiles. One missing University of Vaasa affiliation was verified from a published article and corrected. Louvain clustering at resolution one and seed 534 finds 19 communities among 415 linked institutions; nine remain unconnected. See M5 Section 5.17.
slides.source: ../03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature/AFFILIATIONS.md

slides.title: Affiliation Groups Depend on the Representation
slides.caption: Fractional papers in the six largest of 19 communities. All 745 papers contribute one in total.
slides.description: Bars show C01 154.15, C02 84.54, C03 74.65, C04 67.16, C05 57.80, and C06 48.52 fractional papers. Group membership is based on shared university affiliations, independently of agency coding.
slides.notes: The median adjusted Rand agreement across twenty seeds is 0.522; switching from fractional to full edge counting gives 0.193. These are exploratory communities. The selected mechanism overlay has uneven review coverage and cannot establish institutional intent or rank universities by harm. The full program and all memberships appear in M5 Section 5.17 and the affiliation outputs.
slides.source: ../03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature/AFFILIATIONS.md

slides.title: Coding Exercise: A Label Assessment
bullets: Run the earnings-call assessment and role-exposure calculation.
Test denial, future intention, and a missed paraphrase.
Explain which extra labels would identify precision and recall.
slides.notes: Use ../03_Data_and_Code/Earnings_Calls/README.md and LLM_EXERCISES.md. The mHealth example provides a second application of held-out description evaluation. Synthetic dictionary contrasts are implementation checks; they do not estimate deployment accuracy.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.9, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Engagement and Commercial Value
bullets: Likes and comments measure platform responses.
Sales and contribution require separate outcome records.
Network similarity can reflect common interests or common exposure.
slides.notes: Homophily and shared shocks can generate correlated behavior among connected users. A causal influence claim requires an assignment or identification design beyond a network correlation.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.8, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

slides.title: Authenticity of Reviews and Endorsements
bullets: A generated product description and a claimed customer review serve different roles.
A fabricated experience misrepresents the source of the evidence.
Keep sponsored relationships and substantive editing traceable.
slides.notes: The FTC review rule addresses business conduct involving fake or false reviews. Its FAQ distinguishes mere review hosting from creation, purchase, and dissemination of testimonials, with provision-specific conditions.
slides.source: FTC Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule Q&A. https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers

slides.title: Text-Analysis Discussion
bullets: Which label disagreement would change the service decision?
How does the expected queue change when prevalence falls?
What comparison would distinguish exposure from influence?
slides.notes: A practical assessment prioritizes errors that alter the action. False positives determine review burden, while false negatives determine missed cases. Both should be evaluated in the deployment population.
slides.source: M5, Section 5.9, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md

practice: Assess word exposure and pricing constructs; separate prompt revision from fresh document evaluation.
application: Compare earnings-call labels, mHealth descriptions, and network interpretations on their stated populations.

title: Project Evidence and Midterm Presentations
objectives: Connect a managerial decision to a defensible analytical comparison.
Explain a data assessment, model choice, and consequential uncertainty.
Provide evidence-based feedback on an analysis.

slides.title: A Decision and Its Evidence
bullets: State the action a manager can change.
Define the outcome, population, and horizon.
Identify which evidence could change the proposed action.
slides.notes: A presentation should make the decision assessable without requiring the audience to reconstruct the analyst's workflow. A precise unresolved question is useful when the current evidence does not yet support an action.

slides.title: A Traceable Data Table
bullets: Name the original unit and the analysis unit.
Reconcile rows and totals through joins and restrictions.
Show one manually checked record or aggregate.
slides.notes: A source-to-output assessment distinguishes data processing choices from modeling choices. An unexplained change in the population can dominate a later coefficient or chart.

slides.title: Evidence Categories
bullets: Descriptive patterns summarize observed records.
Prediction evaluates outcomes on held-out observations.
Causal estimates require a justified counterfactual comparison.
Scenarios calculate consequences under imposed inputs.
slides.notes: These categories can appear in the same project. Each claim should retain the qualifications appropriate to its evidence.

slides.title: A Worked Presentation Case
bullets: A paid-plan scenario has high predicted uptake.
The underlying data contain food logging and no observed payments.
The decision requires additional evidence on price, retention, and margin.
slides.notes: Observed logging can motivate a segmentation or interface decision. Paid uptake from an imposed logit model is a scenario. A stated-choice study or pilot could supply some of the missing evidence.
slides.source: M4, Section 4.11, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md

slides.title: An Interpretable Figure
bullets: Use a comparison that answers the stated question.
Label units, denominator, and uncertainty.
State whether plotted quantities are observed, estimated, or imposed.
slides.notes: A figure should be independently readable. A chart of customer means and an interval for the overall mean require separate explanations of distribution and uncertainty.

slides.title: A Reproducible Calculation
bullets: Run from a clean session using documented inputs.
Show a counterexample that checks a consequential choice.
Keep complete code and results linked to the claim.
slides.notes: The most informative check is one that would fail under a plausible analytical error. Re-running identical code is useful but does not independently establish a valid interpretation.

slides.title: Presentation Discussion
bullets: What is the strongest supported claim?
Which assumption most affects the decision?
What evidence should be collected next?
slides.notes: Feedback should identify a concrete comparison or data requirement. A more complicated model is useful only if it addresses a stated limitation in the decision evidence.

slides.title: A Revision Decision
bullets: Prioritize the error with the largest consequence for the action.
Specify the additional data or comparison needed.
Preserve a reproducible baseline for the revised analysis.
slides.notes: Examples include fixing a multiplied join, changing a leakage-prone split, or measuring actual contribution. These changes can matter more than polishing an already clear chart.

slides.title: A Customer-Outcome Evaluation
bullets: Identify who benefits and who can bear a cost.
State whether the optimized metric can conflict with customer value.
Name the relevant jurisdiction and verify the rule's scope.
slides.notes: These questions organize an evidence discussion. They do not establish a graded assignment or replace the eventual project brief.
slides.source: ETHICS_AND_REGULATION.md.

slides.title: Sensitivity and Next Steps
bullets: Report how the action changes across plausible inputs.
Identify a decision threshold rather than only a point estimate.
Select a feasible test that reduces consequential uncertainty.
slides.notes: A recommendation can be conditional. Explicitly stating the value or response threshold makes the condition useful for a manager rather than an abstract caveat.

practice: Presentation blocks and evidence-based discussion; no new graded requirement is introduced.
application: Critique an mHealth paid-plan scenario and identify the next useful evidence.

title: Experiments and Incremental Value
objectives: Define a treatment, assignment unit, outcome, and estimand.
Calculate an intention-to-treat effect, uncertainty, and contribution.
Plan power and use prior outcomes to improve precision.

slides.title: Comparable Markets Receive Different Assignments
slides.description: A merchant sends packages across two separate bridges to comparable villages. Distinct pennants represent treatment assignments.
slides.notes: Random assignment balances potential outcomes in expectation. The comparison still requires well-defined outcomes, complete measurement, and an appropriate unit of assignment.
slides.source: Original conceptual illustration. 05_Slides/assets/PROVENANCE.md.

slides.title: An Email-Campaign Decision
bullets: Eligible customers receive either an email or no email.
Measure purchases over a fixed response window.
The decision concerns contribution per assigned customer.
slides.notes: Assignment remains the denominator even when some customers do not open the email. Conditioning on opening selects a post-assignment group.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Potential Outcomes
slides.intro: For eligible customer $i$, define outcomes with and without assignment.
slides.interpretation: Each customer has one observed outcome under the realized assignment.
slides.notes: The average treatment effect concerns the specified eligible population and treatment implementation. The assignment design supplies the comparison needed to estimate the missing counterfactual mean.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Selection Creates an Alternative Explanation
slides.caption: Randomized assignment is distinct from engagement-driven email opening.
slides.description: A shared determinant can influence both treatment receipt and the outcome, creating a noncausal path. Random assignment removes that systematic selection path under the design.
slides.notes: Control variables should follow the causal structure and timing. Conditioning on a variable affected by treatment can change the estimand or introduce selection.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Email Assignment and Purchase
slides.caption: Synthetic experiment. Each customer has one binary outcome.
slides.notes: The difference is three percentage points. Relative to a 10% control rate, that equals a 30% relative increase. The two descriptions use different denominators.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: An Assignment-Effect Estimate
slides.intro: Compare purchase rates across all assigned customers.
slides.interpretation: The estimated effect is three additional purchases per 100 assigned customers.
slides.notes: This is an intention-to-treat comparison under the stated randomized design. An opened-email comparison would use a different selected population.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Sampling Uncertainty
slides.intro: Use an independent-group approximation for the synthetic binary outcomes.
slides.interpretation: An approximate 95% interval is 0.21 to 5.79 percentage points.
slides.notes: The interval uses a large-sample normal approximation and independent customer assignments. It does not include systematic outcome measurement errors or interference.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Contribution and Decision Uncertainty
bullets: An extra purchase contributes 40 dollars.
Delivery costs 0.50 dollars per assigned customer.
Estimated incremental contribution is 0.70 dollars per customer.
slides.notes: The same transformation of the effect interval gives approximately -0.42 to 1.82 dollars. The calculation assumes no additional discount cost and fixed contribution per additional purchase.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: The Experiment Calculation
slides.intro: Reproduce the effect and its contribution implication.
slides.code:
from math import sqrt
p1, p0, n = 0.13, 0.10, 1000
effect = p1 - p0
se = sqrt(p1*(1-p1)/n + p0*(1-p0)/n)
interval = (effect - 1.96*se, effect + 1.96*se)
profit = 40 * effect - 0.50
assert round(profit, 2) == 0.70
slides.check: The point estimate is positive while the contribution interval includes losses.
slides.notes: If treatment changes basket size, returns, or margins, purchase incidence alone no longer gives the contribution effect. Measuring contribution directly can better match the decision.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Power Begins With the Useful Effect
bullets: Choose the smallest effect that could change the action.
Use the expected outcome variance and assignment unit.
Halving the target effect approximately quadruples sample size.
slides.notes: At baseline probability 0.10, a two-point effect, two-sided 5% level, and 80% power, a common-variance normal approximation gives 3,528 customers per arm.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Implementation Checks
bullets: Reconcile assigned counts and intended allocation.
Check missing outcomes and tracking by assignment.
Preserve the planned outcome horizon.
Investigate exclusions that depend on treatment response.
slides.notes: A randomization protocol does not prevent differential tracking failures. Sample-ratio discrepancies can reveal implementation problems. Chance covariate imbalance alone does not invalidate a correctly implemented randomization.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.6, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Prior Outcomes and Precision
slides.intro: Adjust the outcome using a pre-treatment measure $X$.
slides.interpretation: A predictive baseline can reduce residual variation while preserving the assignment comparison.
slides.notes: CUPED uses a pre-treatment covariate and an appropriately specified adjustment. The variance reduction does not create treatment variation or repair selection into treatment.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.15, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: mHealth Baseline Activity Improves Precision
slides.caption: Planning calculation uses historical user-level variance and a five-point target.
slides.description: The detectable-change curves compare unadjusted and prior-period-adjusted logging outcomes. The indicated sample sizes are 788 and 397 independent users per arm under the stated approximation.
slides.notes: These are power-planning implications of observed historical variances, not a realized intervention effect. The future population, outcome process, and assignment need to match the planning conditions.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.15, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Model and Library Contributions
slides.caption: Synthetic counts: 100 assigned tasks per condition; common rubric and resource limits.
slides.description: Without the library, passing tasks rise from 60% with the earlier model to 65% with the newer model. With the library, they rise from 70% to 85%. The library gain increases from 10 to 20 percentage points.
slides.notes: The interaction is ten percentage points. Moving from the initial condition to the newer model with the library improves the imposed rate by twenty-five points. Independent assignments, valid reference outcomes, and fresh tasks would be required for an empirical causal comparison. These counts are constructed, with unfinished tasks counted as failures.
slides.source: Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes, M6 §6.19.

slides.title: An Interaction Calculation
slides.intro: The four rates are imposed teaching inputs.
slides.code:
q00, q01, q10, q11 = 0.60, 0.70, 0.65, 0.85
model_alone = q10 - q00
library_after_model = q11 - q10
interaction = (q11-q10) - (q01-q00)
assert round(interaction, 2) == 0.10
assert round(model_alone + library_after_model, 2) == 0.25
slides.check: A joint gain does not uniquely allocate the interaction to either component.
slides.notes: Run factorial.py to reproduce both paths to the joint change using exact rational arithmetic. Randomize at the team or project level when outputs share personnel, prompts, or helper code. Record actual cost alongside pass rates and resource ceilings.
slides.source: M6 §6.19. ../03_Data_and_Code/AI_Workflows/factorial.py

bullets: Compute the factorial contrasts alongside the email effect.
Change contribution, delivery cost, and the target effect.

slides.title: Interference and Assignment Units
bullets: Customers can share offers or affect one another.
Stores can divert purchases from nearby locations.
The assignment unit should reflect the likely spillovers.
slides.notes: If one treated store gains by taking business from a comparison store, the store-level difference can exceed the chain-wide gain. Cluster assignment changes both interpretation and precision.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.10, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: A Treatment Arm Needs a Defensible Design
bullets: Random assignment identifies a comparison.
The content of each treatment still affects the customers who receive it.
Include customer outcomes, refusal, and stopping conditions.
slides.notes: Randomization does not establish that a deceptive or harmful interface is acceptable. Separate analytical identification from the substantive and regulatory evaluation of each proposed treatment.
slides.source: ETHICS_AND_REGULATION.md, M6.

slides.title: Follow Purchases Through Returns
bullets: Pressure and self-assurance can produce different purchase and return patterns.
Prespecify the eligible population and both outcome horizons.
For cancellation, measure intent, completion, and subsequent charges.
slides.notes: The verified abstract of the randomized online-retailing study reports stronger purchase responses alongside more returns under pressure nudges. Its full text remains unavailable in the collection. The directional result motivates balanced outcomes; exact effects and implementation details require the complete paper. A cancellation study should define eligibility at the initial request and compare lawful designs. See M6 Section 6.20.

slides.title: Experiment Discussion
bullets: Would a conversion gain cover the campaign cost?
What changes if only email openers enter the analysis?
Which guardrail outcome could reverse the rollout decision?
slides.notes: Contribution uncertainty remains consequential even with a positive purchase effect. Returns, satisfaction, and service burden can alter the decision. The outcome set should reflect the intervention.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.11, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

title: Causal Comparisons and Policy Evaluation
objectives: Explain the identifying comparison in difference-in-differences, RD, and IV.
Evaluate a policy under selected exposure and support restrictions.
Assess whether a comparison group is suitable for the McBroken policy question.

slides.title: A Repair-Policy Question
bullets: A policy may change the cost of restoring restaurant availability.
A national before-after change also includes common shocks.
The target is the change attributable to the policy over a defined horizon.
slides.notes: The McBroken setting motivates a causal question. The supplied panel does not by itself establish a valid untreated comparison for a policy affecting the same environment broadly.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.16, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Difference-in-Differences
slides.intro: Subtract the comparison group's change from the treated group's change.
slides.interpretation: Parallel untreated trends connect the observed changes to a causal effect.
slides.notes: Different starting levels can be compatible with the design. The assumption concerns untreated changes, not identical outcome levels.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.8, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: The Counterfactual Trend
slides.caption: Synthetic outcomes. Treated sales rise 120 to 150 and comparison sales 100 to 110.
slides.description: The implied untreated treated-group outcome is 130. The observed treated outcome is 150, giving a 20-unit difference.
slides.notes: The dashed path is an implied counterfactual. A treatment-specific demand shock at the same time would challenge the interpretation.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.8, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Design Checks
bullets: Examine pre-treatment outcomes and institutional timing.
Consider anticipation, spillovers, and changing composition.
Match the comparison group to the policy's untreated counterfactual.
slides.notes: A nonsignificant pre-trend test does not establish parallel trends. With staggered adoption and heterogeneous effects, the choice of comparison groups and aggregation becomes especially important.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.8, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: McBroken and the Comparison Group
slides.caption: A policy-analysis design requires a credible untreated comparison.
slides.description: The figure distinguishes the proposed policy timing from restaurant coverage and observed availability. A national time change alone mixes the policy with other changes.
slides.notes: The course case retains missing dates and unknown statuses. Those measurement issues should be addressed before interpreting an apparent policy break.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.16, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Fewer Mentions Can Leave Incidence Unchanged
slides.caption: Observed calls around February 27, 2024; same comparison firms in both windows.
slides.description: In 90-day windows excluding the event day, the same 27 comparison firms have 27 calls each side. Occurrences fall from five to two, while two positive calls each side imply 7.41%.
slides.notes: The event is Wendy's dated public clarification of digital-menu intentions. In all available comparison calls, incidence falls from 2/27 to 2/34 as coverage expands. The firm group name does not establish an untreated counterfactual.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.18, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: A Public Event Does Not Assign Treatment
bullets: Define the window, event-day exclusion, and observed-call denominator.
Compare common firms and alternative window lengths.
A causal claim needs exposure, a counterfactual, and a specified outcome.
slides.notes: Run event_windows.py for 60-, 90-, and 120-day comparisons with call and firm weights. A change in communication is distinct from a change in pricing behavior or customer outcomes. Matching coverage removes one composition difference, not concurrent shocks.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.18, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Regression Discontinuity
bullets: Eligibility can change at a known score threshold.
Nearby units require continuity of other outcome determinants.
The resulting effect is local to the cutoff and compliance behavior.
slides.notes: Manipulation of the score and discontinuities in other policies threaten the comparison. Bandwidth and functional form should be assessed within the design.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.9, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Instrumental Variables
bullets: The instrument shifts treatment or price.
Exclusion restricts its other paths to the outcome.
Relevance alone does not establish exclusion.
slides.notes: Under the appropriate binary-treatment conditions, IV can identify a local effect for compliers. The interpretation depends on the assignment mechanism and monotonicity, as well as the first stage.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.9, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Recommendation Logs Select Exposure
bullets: Frequent buyers may usually see product A.
Occasional buyers may usually see product B.
Their raw click rates compare different customer populations.
slides.notes: A logged outcome is observed after a selected display. A policy comparison must account for the distribution of customers and actions that generated those observations.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.7.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Exposure Adjustment Reverses the Ranking
slides.caption: Synthetic randomized logging within frequent and occasional buyer groups.
slides.description: Raw click rates favor A, 56% versus 41%. A common equally weighted population favors B, 45% versus 40%.
slides.notes: The constructed logging design gives A probability 0.90 for frequent buyers and 0.10 for occasional buyers. B receives the complement. The common-population comparison holds customer mix fixed.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.7.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Inverse-Propensity Policy Value
slides.intro: Weight each observed outcome by target-policy probability over logging probability.
slides.interpretation: The denominator counts every eligible logged opportunity.
slides.notes: Identification requires the relevant exchangeability condition and positive logging support wherever the target policy acts. A randomized logging policy can supply known assignment probabilities.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.7.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: A Common-Population Calculation
slides.intro: Synthetic clicks and logging probabilities identify the two policy values.
slides.check: The raw ranking and policy-value ranking disagree.
slides.notes: An independent check averages the two group-specific response rates under equal population weights. The small-probability cells receive large weights and contribute substantial uncertainty.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.7.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Support and Weight Concentration
bullets: An action never shown to a group has no observed outcome there.
Large weights amplify a small number of records.
Clipping changes the estimator and its bias-variance tradeoff.
slides.notes: Zero support cannot be repaired by increasing a weight. Weight-concentration summaries are diagnostics and do not replace a variance calculation that respects dependence.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.7.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Spillovers Change the Outcome Comparison
slides.caption: Synthetic store network with effects beyond assigned units.
slides.description: A treated store can attract customers from a nearby comparison store. The difference between stores then mixes the direct effect with displacement.
slides.notes: The chain-wide outcome may change less than the treated-store outcome. Assignment and outcome aggregation should follow the managerial decision.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.10, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: Information and Exposure
bullets: A recommendation can draw attention to an item.
A personalized endorsement can also change beliefs.
Separate interventions can identify these channels.
slides.notes: The MovieLens experiment discussed in the notes distinguishes recommendation and exposure-only conditions. The relevant outcome and information treatment should be stated before attributing a response to personalization.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.10.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

slides.title: A Policy Value for Whom?
bullets: Clicks and sales can rise while customer value falls.
A causal estimate concerns the outcome that was actually measured.
Record refusal, completion, and customer time when procedures change.
slides.notes: A valid causal effect on conversion does not identify the welfare effect without information about customer values and costs. The next measurement should address the missing part of the decision.
slides.source: ETHICS_AND_REGULATION.md, M6.

slides.title: Causal-Design Discussion
bullets: What would the treated group have experienced without the policy?
Which group or action lacks comparable support?
What institutional evidence strengthens the proposed comparison?
slides.notes: A causal interpretation rests on the comparison and assumptions. A flexible estimator does not supply a missing assignment mechanism or recover outcomes outside support.
slides.source: M6, Section 6.11, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md

title: Prediction, Validation, and Marketing Actions
objectives: Design a holdout that matches deployment and prevents leakage.
Compare ranking, calibration, and decision costs.
Assess coverage and missing future labels in an availability forecast.

slides.title: A Service-Capacity Decision
bullets: A team can review 100 customers each week.
Predictions use information available before that week.
The outcome and review benefit determine the useful metric.
slides.notes: A model selected on overall accuracy can fail to identify the cases that the team can help. The intervention value and the forecast are separate quantities.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Validation Reproduces Deployment
slides.caption: The deployment population determines the appropriate holdout.
slides.description: Random rows, whole-customer holdouts, and later-period holdouts test different forms of generalization.
slides.notes: New-customer prediction requires separation by customer. Future prediction for returning customers requires separation in time. Some deployments require both.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Selection on Development Accuracy
slides.caption: Synthetic independent chance predictions: 80 development cases per candidate.
slides.description: Expected selected development accuracy rises from 50% for one candidate to 56.49%, 60.40%, and 63.93% for five, twenty, and one hundred candidates. Expected fresh accuracy stays at 50%.
slides.notes: Each candidate has true accuracy one-half under the imposed independent Bernoulli model. The maximum development score increases with the number compared. Fresh test correctness is independent of selection. The program verifies the analytic expectation and simulates 2,000 repetitions with 200 test cases. Real prompt candidates can be correlated, so the magnitude is illustrative.
slides.source: Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes, M7 §7.20.

slides.title: The Forecast Origin
bullets: Features end before the decision time.
The outcome window begins after the decision.
Training labels must already be observable at fitting time.
slides.notes: A database extract can contain information that did not exist at the historical prediction origin. Store measurement windows or feature timestamps to make the information constraint verifiable.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.1, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Baselines and Model Families
bullets: Compare with a constant probability or recent-history forecast.
Logistic regression supplies a probability baseline.
Trees represent conditional splits. Ensembles combine trees.
slides.notes: A complex model earns its place through performance on the intended held-out observations and decision costs. Training fit alone rewards flexibility.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Logistic Prediction
slides.intro: Transform a linear index into a binary-outcome probability.
slides.interpretation: A coefficient changes log odds. Its probability effect depends on the starting point.
slides.notes: The same index change has a larger probability effect near the middle than near zero or one. Calibration should be evaluated on the deployment population.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.3, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Preprocessing Belongs in Training
bullets: Fit imputation, scaling, and vocabulary on training records.
Choose model settings using validation data.
Keep the final test sample separate from model selection.
slides.notes: Repeatedly choosing features from test performance turns that sample into validation data. A pipeline helps preserve the training-only boundary within cross-validation.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.4, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Rare Purchases and Accuracy
slides.caption: Synthetic population: 1,000 customers and 50 purchases.
slides.notes: Flagging 100 customers gives precision 30%, recall 60%, and accuracy 91%. Predicting no purchase for everybody gives 95% accuracy and finds no purchasers.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Metrics and the Review Queue
bullets: Precision: what fraction of reviewed cases are positive?
Recall: what fraction of positives enter the queue?
Calibration: do predicted probabilities match observed frequencies?
slides.notes: The appropriate contact fraction should match staff capacity. A ranking measure and a probability measure answer different questions. Neither by itself measures the causal effect of contacting a customer.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.6, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Ranking Can Stay Fixed While Probabilities Change
slides.caption: A synthetic transformation squares initially calibrated probabilities.
slides.description: Squaring the scores preserves their order but changes the probability scale. Ranking performance can remain unchanged while expected counts become wrong.
slides.notes: For q=p squared, the original outcome frequency p equals the square root of q. Expected contribution calculations need probabilities with the relevant interpretation.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.6, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: A Cost-Based Threshold
slides.intro: Suppose false positives cost $C_{FP}$ and false negatives cost $C_{FN}$.
slides.interpretation: With costs 1 and 9, the threshold is 0.10 under this simplified classification loss.
slides.notes: Correct classifications have zero cost in this example. Capacity constraints and different action effects require a richer decision model.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.7, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Coupon Targeting Includes the Untreated Outcome
slides.caption: Synthetic probabilities and costs. High treated response can have negative incremental value.
slides.description: Customer A has treated purchase probability 0.80 and contribution -5.20 dollars. B has probability 0.30 and contribution 2.50 dollars under the stated coupon model.
slides.notes: Contribution is 40 dollars, discount 5 dollars per treated purchase, and contact cost 2 dollars. Baseline probabilities are 0.78 and 0.15. Discount expense applies to purchases that would also have occurred without the coupon.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.8, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Queue Metrics
slides.intro: Compute metrics from the synthetic confusion matrix.
slides.code:
tp, fn, fp, tn = 30, 20, 70, 880
precision = tp / (tp + fp)
recall = tp / (tp + fn)
accuracy = (tp + tn) / (tp + fn + fp + tn)
assert (precision, recall, accuracy) == (0.3, 0.6, 0.91)
slides.check: The model finds 60% of purchasers while 70% of its queue contains nonpurchasers.
slides.notes: Whether that queue is profitable depends on the action and its incremental outcome. A prediction score alone cannot supply the causal response to a coupon.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.5, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: McBroken Forecasting
bullets: Predict availability on a later date.
Retain a separate count of unknown future labels.
Compare baseline and fitted forecasts on the same observed outcomes.
slides.notes: An unknown future status is not an observed available restaurant. Dropping missing labels changes the evaluated population and can make an apparently strong forecast depend on observation coverage.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.18, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Prediction and Outcome Coverage
slides.caption: McBroken forecasts use later dates and observed-label denominators.
slides.description: The figure compares forecast performance while preserving the distinction between known labels and missing future outcomes.
slides.notes: The course example checks information availability at the forecast origin and uses chronological evaluation. Missing outcome counts remain alongside accuracy measures.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.18.2, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md

slides.title: Accuracy and Failure Costs
slides.caption: Constructed cases: pooled accuracy rises from 78% to 86%.
slides.description: Routine accuracy rises from 75% to 90% on eighty cases; consequential accuracy falls from 90% to 70% on twenty.
slides.notes: Fourteen paired cases improve and six regress. Stipulated failure costs of one dollar for routine tasks and twenty dollars for consequential tasks give losses of sixty and 128 dollars. The additional four consequential failures outweigh the twelve avoided routine failures. These are constructed values, not measured model performance.
slides.source: M7 §7.22. ../03_Data_and_Code/LLM_Revalidation/README.md

slides.title: Paired Regression Checks
slides.intro: The same one hundred constructed cases are scored under both configurations.
slides.code:
improved, regressed, cases = 14, 6, 100
gain_pp = 100 * (improved - regressed) / cases
old_loss = 20 * 1 + 2 * 20
new_loss = 8 * 1 + 6 * 20
print(gain_pp, old_loss, new_loss)
slides.check: Output: 8.0 percentage points; current loss 60 dollars; challenger loss 128 dollars.
slides.notes: The complete program preserves every paired case and each segment denominator. With a consequential-to-routine loss ratio q, the change in failure loss is -12 + 4q. The challenger improves this loss only below a ratio of three. Inference fees, setup costs, and other outcomes require additional terms.
slides.source: M7 §7.22. ../03_Data_and_Code/LLM_Revalidation/evaluate_upgrade.py

bullets: Compare development and fresh accuracy after candidate selection.
Check every feature against the forecast date.
Compare a simple baseline, ranking, and calibration.
Report missing outcomes beside the test metrics.

Use the McBroken forecasting scripts for the real-panel extension, following their README and saved outcome definitions. The AI_Workflows folder supplies complete standard-library calculations with synthetic inputs.

slides.title: Targeting and Delivered Opportunities
bullets: An apparently neutral target can produce unequal delivery.
Evaluate exposure and error costs across relevant groups.
Housing, credit, and employment applications require their specific legal context.
slides.notes: The DOJ's Meta housing-ad settlement addresses discriminatory delivery as well as targeting tools. That case is evidence about housing advertising and should not be generalized into a single rule for all products.

slides.title: Prediction Discussion
bullets: Which error uses scarce review capacity?
Which feature becomes available too late?
Does the score support a forecast, an intervention, or both?
slides.notes: A deployment decision needs an explicit chain from information to prediction to action. Each link has its own empirical requirements.
slides.source: M7, Section 7.9, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md
